answer: An agent economy can price Sybil risk like insurance: every identity pays a premium into a mutual pool, set by a shared kernel risk model that tracks how often an identity's cluster misbehaves. Honest agents in a quiet dune of the network pay almost nothing, while a cluster that spawns lookalikes sees premiums climb steeply for all of them at once. Each fake still costs a real premium, and correlated fraud makes the next fake pricier than the last, so a farm's bill grows faster than its army — an opal of clean history is the cheapest asset an agent owns.
